problem: Learned PDDL domains (e.g. UniDomain) are limited to tabletop manipulation, and existing LLM/VLM planners either lose visual information via text scene graphs, are mapless with few images, or fail on long-horizon constraints and cost-aware navigation in large indoor environments.
motivation: Long-horizon mobile manipulation in large real-world spaces requires preserving task-dependent visual detail, enforcing hard operational constraints (hands, doors) and scaling to hundreds of images. Combining VLM grounding with a symbolic planner over a unified navigation+manipulation domain gives robustness and optimality without mobile demonstrations.
key_idea: Programmatically extend learned tabletop PDDL domains with navigation, doors, bimanual and cost via AST rewrites, and build a factored PDDL problem (VLM grounds objects only from retrieved anchored images, map/robot facts injected programmatically) over a task-compressed visual-topological map solved by Fast Downward.
insight: Factoring is what makes VLM grounding reliable: letting the VLM write the whole problem including topology drops SR to 31.0% in Single-Arm/Door and doubles thinking time. Topology compression is needed for solver tractability (T_plan 0.42s→48.17s without it), the unified domain mostly improves plan quality (RPQG up to 23.6%) rather than SR, and replacing images with text scene graphs loses ~11 SR points (83.75→72.5 average).
method: Programmatic domain expansion: parse the PDDL domain into an AST via the Unified Planning framework and apply deterministic rewrite rules keyed on semantic anchors (hand_free ?r), (holding ?r ?o); domain-agnostic and reusable.
Navigation/door expansion: add ?n parameter, rob_at_node/obj_at_node preconditions and effects (pick removes obj_at_node, place adds it), plus connected, has_door, move_robot and open_door operators.

Bimanual expansion and cost modeling: lift anchors to hand-specific (hand_free ?r ?h), (holding ?r ?h ?o) with rob_has_hand; travel_cost accumulates in move_robot, constant cost 1 for manipulation, cost-optimal metric.
Visual-topological map: pose, room and asset nodes; asset nodes anchored with high-resolution images; built offline (43 pose, 18 room, 18 doors, 31 asset nodes, 100+ objects).

Task-oriented map compression: VLM captions as a text index, LLM selects relevant asset nodes; Dijkstra shortcut edges with true travel costs between selected nodes and robot location, no shortcuts through closed doors, waypoints cached for later refinement.

Factored problem formation: robot state injected programmatically; VLM grounds objects, initial states and goal from retrieved images (forbidden from robot predicates); topology, costs and door states injected; Fast Downward seq-opt-lmcut solves; abstract moves expanded to waypoints.

setting.backbone: GPT-5.2 (frozen, temperature 0, no reasoning) as VLM/LLM plus Fast Downward seq-opt-lmcut; UniDomain-learned PDDL base domain (81 operators, 79 predicates)
setting.training_data: none (training-free); reuses pre-learned UniDomain PDDL domain
setting.observation: pre-built visual-topological map with anchored high-resolution RGB images at asset nodes; robot state from onboard perception
setting.action_space: high-level symbolic PDDL actions (pick, place, open, pour, move_robot, open_door, etc.) with hand parameters, refined to waypoints
setting.simulator: custom Python task-environment emulator built on a real-world indoor map (perfect low-level execution assumed)
setting.privileged: pre-built offline visual-topological map of the environment; static fully observable environment; perfect low-level execution

numbers_note: Custom benchmark (50 tasks on own map), not a standard navigation benchmark; baselines omitted per rules. Ablation numbers exist in Table 2 but are not listed.
results: UniPlan reaches 82.0–85.5% SR (avg 83.75%) across four settings with only 2 LLM calls and ~21 s thinking time, versus best baseline SayPlan at 33.0–49.5% and DELTA 18.5–26.5%. Plans are shorter than baselines (RPQG ~2–16%) and symbolic planning takes <0.7 s.
limitations: Dual arms modeled as logically independent, so no synchronized bimanual manipulation.
Assumes a static, fully observable environment and a pre-built map; no handling of dynamic changes or occlusion.
Evaluated only in an emulator with perfect low-level execution on one map; ~16% failures from PDDL grounding, perception and retrieval errors.
